title: Current fused INT8 decoder batch4 versus batch8: rejected exactness screen
conclusion: The batch8 configuration did not pass the exact RGB gate. No performance measurement, fresh encode validation or production change followed.
scope_limitations: This is configuration tuning using the unchanged production fused kernel, not a kernel optimization.
The same cached FP16 latent from an earlier primary-video profiling run is used for both configurations; this is not fresh full-video encoding validation.
One compiled decoder object naturally specializes separately for batch4 and batch8; no normalization object is reused across shapes.
Read-only Python observers around tile scheduling and the opaque FFN implementation record validation coverage. No tensor arithmetic is changed by those observers.
Because the first complete RGB comparison failed, the planned observer-free confirmation, warmups, paired timing and fresh-video stages were not run.
The numerical difference was not localized to a specific operator. Shape-specific reduction or GEMM schedules are possibilities, not proven causes.
No batch16 experiment and no normalization or numerical-contract relaxation was attempted.

scope: targeted earlier decoder FFN temporary reports
history_audit.finding: No real current-fused INT8 batch8 or batch16 full decode was found before this screen. Published M14376 quantizer followup used repeated rows. Earlier batch8 VAE records inspected were FP16; actual INT8 records inspected used batch2 or batch4.
history_audit.limit: No stable historical INT8 batch8 failure was found within this bounded search; the search was not exhaustive across external directories.

raw_screen.scope:
Bounded current INT8 fused decoder batch4 versus batch8 configuration check.

Same runtime/checkpoint/input/tile/precision; shape-specific compiler choices are
left unchanged. Full RGB exactness is a hard gate before any timing. This is
configuration tuning, not a kernel optimization or an FP16 quality comparison.
notes: Both variants use the current production fused FFN-up kernel.
One runtime and one compiled decoder object; separate natural shape specializations.
Tile batching closures each wrap the same original tile task method once.
Observers collect actual tile batches and 36 FFN weights only during quality.
No observers, module hooks, norm bindings, or custom-op substitutions during timing.
Compilation, loading, FP16 encoding and all validation are excluded from timing.
Cached input is a local screen; fresh same-video encoding is required for formal validation.
Any RGB mismatch stops this configuration experiment before timing.
This configuration comparison does not establish a new kernel speedup.
Peak memory includes resident model, both compiled shape caches and one result.
